findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded as plaintext Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. Anyone with access to the repository, the Terraform state, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can read these long-lived credentials and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

The Lambda function stores sensitive values in environment variables without specifying a customer-managed KMS key (kms_key_arn); environment variables are only protected by the default AWS-managed key and are visible in plaintext to any principal that can describe the function.
No tracing_config block is set, so request tracing is disabled, reducing the forensic/audit trail available when investigating abuse of the function.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a deprecated runtime that no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config is defined, so the function runs outside a customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group-based egress control, which can facilitate data exfiltration if the code is compromised.
